title: Ordinary completed coefficient tensor balancing and exactness
statement: For a scheme X and adic datum d on a commutative ring A [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], let E be the actual ordinary completed scalar extension and H its composite with exact constant realization [lem-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-adic-free-tensor-cone]. Then E preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Let T(M)_n=M tensor_A A/I^(n+1) with actual quotient transitions [lem-weil-pbc-adic-ordinary-tensor-levels], and let B_n be the actual finite coefficient module over the completed ring. There is an isomorphism H(M) tensor_(A_T) B_n ≅ H(T(M)_n), natural simultaneously in the A-module M and in all quotient transitions. Equivalently these comparisons form a natural isomorphism between the two functors from A-modules to diagrams of completed module sheaves. There is no complex or derived-functor assertion.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating family for the ideal and lift it to ULift A. Reuse the proved completionRingIso and its scalar normalization from CompletedKoszulFiniteQuotientComparison to identify the prescribed completed ring with the completion of the lifted constant algebra. Apply completed_constant_algebra_flat_quotients and exactFunctor_iff to obtain preservation of finite limits and finite colimits.

For each quotient, transport the normalized quotientModuleIso_exists comparison from CompletedKoszulFiniteQuotientComparison through liftedQuotientEquiv. Its normalization identifies the image of A to A/I^(n+1) with finitePerfectAdicCoefficientProjection. Since constant realization and completed scalar extension preserve finite colimits, the image of A to A/I^(m+1) is an epimorphism. Cancel this epimorphism and the regular-unit isomorphism to prove naturality for every quotient transition. This gives a natural isomorphism from the realized ordinary coefficient diagram to the actual finite coefficient diagram.

Identify the ordinary ringed constant-module realization, after restriction to fixed scalars, with the fixed-coefficient constant-sheaf functor. Construct the comparison from the sheafification unit; its scalar linearity follows from restriction_scalar, and local bijectivity makes it an isomorphism. Transport the monoidal structure of constant sheafification through the monoidal scalar-restriction equivalence. Combine its tensor comparison with the explicit ULift tensor equivalence and the scalarExtension_constraint_coherence comparison (transported through the recorded object and map equalities for completedAdicScalarExtension).

For a module M and a coefficient index n, tensor the inverse coefficient comparison with H(M), then apply the inverse tensor comparison H(M) tensor H(Q_n) to H(M tensor Q_n). The coefficient comparison naturality and tensor comparison naturality prove naturality in n; whisker exchange and tensor comparison naturality prove naturality in M. Package these equations using two applications of NatIso.ofComponents. Apply the resulting natural isomorphism degreewise to obtain the existing complex comparison.

theorem finitePerfectAdicOrdinaryCoefficient_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) :
    (PreservesFiniteLimits (completedAdicScalarExtension X d) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (completedAdicScalarExtension X d)) ∧
    Nonempty (finitePerfectAdicOrdinary X d ⋙ finitePerfectAdicTensorFunctor X d ≅
      adicOrdinaryTensorFunctor d.ideal ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ (ModuleCat.{t} A) (CompletedAdicModules X d)).obj
          (finitePerfectAdicOrdinary X d))
